```{r}
tree <- read.tree("../data/phyliptree.phy")

tree$tip.label <- str_remove_all(tree$tip.label, "'")

ggtree(tree) + 
  geom_tiplab() +
  theme_tree2()

tree <- read.delim("../data/ncbi_datasets.tsv")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Prepare taxonomic path from your dataframe
# Ordering levels from broad (Phylum) down to Species
tax_df <- tree %>%
  select(Phylum.name, Class.name, Order.name, Family.name, Genus.name, Tax.name) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

# Convert taxonomy table to a phylo tree structure using ape
tax_formula <- ~Phylum.name/Class.name/Order.name/Family.name/Genus.name/Tax.name
phylo_tree <- as.phylo(tax_formula, data = tax_df, shrink = TRUE)

# Set equal branch lengths for a clean cladogram aesthetic
phylo_tree$edge.length <- rep(1, nrow(phylo_tree$edge))

# 2. Visualize with ggtree
p <- ggtree(phylo_tree, branch.length = "none", size = 1) +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = paste0("  ", label)), fontface = "italic", offset = 0.1) +
  theme_tree2() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.4))); p

# 3. Add node annotations to highlight Bilaterian/Cnidarian divergence and Anthozoa/Scleractinia
p + 
  # Highlight the Cnidaria clade
  geom_hilight(node = MRCA(phylo_tree, "Acropora hyacinthus", "Nematostella vectensis"), 
               fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15) +
  # Add clade markers for key taxonomic nodes
  geom_cladelab(node = MRCA(phylo_tree, "Acropora hyacinthus", "Nematostella vectensis"), 
                label = "Cnidaria (Anthozoa)", align = TRUE, offset = 1.2, barcolor = "steelblue") +
  geom_cladelab(node = MRCA(phylo_tree, "Acropora hyacinthus", "Astrangia poculata"), 
                label = "Scleractinia", align = TRUE, offset = 0.8, barcolor = "darkorange") +
  geom_cladelab(node = nodeid(phylo_tree, "Homo sapiens"), 
                label = "Bilateria (Chordata)", align = TRUE, offset = 1.2, barcolor = "darkgreen")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Prepare taxonomic dataframe
tax_df <- tree %>%
  select(Phylum.name, Class.name, Order.name, Family.name, Genus.name, Tax.name) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.factor))

# 2. Build phylo tree
tax_formula <- ~Phylum.name/Class.name/Order.name/Family.name/Genus.name/Tax.name
phylo_tree <- as.phylo(tax_formula, data = tax_df, shrink = TRUE)
phylo_tree$edge.length <- rep(1, nrow(phylo_tree$edge))

# 3. Base plot with expanded x-axis limits to prevent text truncation
p <- ggtree(phylo_tree, branch.length = "none", size = 1) +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = paste0("  ", label)), fontface = "italic", offset = 0.05) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 6.5)) +
  theme_tree();p

# 4. Find internal nodes dynamically
cnidaria_node    <- MRCA(phylo_tree, "Acropora hyacinthus", "Nematostella vectensis")
scleractinia_node <- MRCA(phylo_tree, "Acropora hyacinthus", "Astrangia poculata")
human_node       <- nodeid(phylo_tree, "Homo sapiens")

# 5. Add clean annotations, staggered clade bars, and node labels
p + 
  # Shaded highlight box over Cnidaria
  geom_hilight(node = cnidaria_node, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.12) +
  
  # Inner Clade Bar: Scleractinia
  geom_cladelab(node = scleractinia_node, label = "Scleractinia", 
                align = TRUE, offset = 1.3, barcolor = "#E69F00", 
                barsize = 1.2, textcolor = "#E69F00", fontsize = 4.5) +
                
  # Outer Clade Bar: Cnidaria (Anthozoa)
  geom_cladelab(node = cnidaria_node, label = "Cnidaria (Anthozoa)", 
                align = TRUE, offset = 2.3, barcolor = "steelblue", 
                barsize = 1.2, textcolor = "steelblue", fontsize = 4.5) +
                
  # Label for Bilateria (Chordata)
  geom_cladelab(node = human_node, label = "Bilateria (Chordata)", 
                align = TRUE, offset = 2.3, barcolor = "darkgreen", 
                barsize = 1.2, textcolor = "darkgreen", fontsize = 4.5)
```
